title: Pricing the Unprovable: Ambiguity, Turnstile Runs, and the Verifiability Discount in Crypto Protocols
abstract: arXiv:2610.21540v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Privacy-preserving protocols can repair a vulnerability without establishing whether it was exploited beforehand, even when no theft is reported and aggregate supply is protected. We call the potential value reduction from this gap the verifiability discount. A turnstile model shows how early withdrawal can shift a possible shortfall to remaining holders and why credible evidence can become more valuable as exposure grows. We introduce VDISC, a reproducible framework that records reported loss, exposed value, public evidence, returns, and pool flows separately. It combines Orchard's staged disclosures with reconstructed on-chain flows, earlier Zcash cases, and a 40-event security panel. Orchard follows the predicted direction: market responses were muted after repair and supply assurance, while the largest negative return and aggregate shielded-pool net outflow aligned with the acknowledgment that past abuse could not be ruled out. translated_title: 为不可证明之物定价：加密协议中的模糊性、旋转门式挤兑与可验证性折价
translated_abstract: 隐私保护协议可以在未事先确认漏洞是否已被利用的情况下完成修复，即使没有任何盗窃报告且总供应量得到保护。我们将这种不确定性差距所导致的潜在价值下降称为“可验证性折价”。一个旋转门模型展示了早期提款如何将可能出现的资金缺口转移给剩余持有者，以及为什么随着风险敞口的扩大，可信证据会变得愈发有价值。我们提出了VDISC，一个可复现的框架，分别记录报告损失、风险敞口价值、公开证据、市场回报和资金池流动。该框架将Orchard的分阶段披露与重构的链上资金流、更早的Zcash案例以及包含40个事件的安全性面板相结合。Orchard的实证结果符合预测方向：在完成修复和供应量保障之后，市场反应较为温和，而最大的负回报与屏蔽资金池的整体净流出，恰好对应于官方承认“无法排除过往滥用可能性”的时点。
tldr: 该论文提出“可验证性折价”概念及VDISC可复现分析框架，通过旋转门模型与Zcash/Orchard的链上实证研究表明：当加密货币隐私协议无法证明漏洞是否曾被利用时，市场会对其价值进行折价定价。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "verifiability discount" concept and a reproducible VDISC framework, showing through a turnstile model and Zcash/Orchard on-chain evidence that markets price a discount on crypto privacy protocols when they cannot prove whether a vulnerability was previously exploited.
